knowledge:
- key_parameters: <from=Genomic coordinate defining the start of the plotting window ;; to=Genomic coordinate defining the end of the plotting window ;; extend.left=Numeric zoom factor (between -1 and 1) or absolute base-pair value to extend the plot range to the left ;; extend.right=Numeric zoom factor (between -1 and 1) or absolute base-pair value to extend the plot range to the right ;; type=Character vector specifying the visualization type (e.g., "histogram", "boxplot", "heatmap", "horizon" for DataTrack; "coverage", "sashimi", "pileup" for AlignmentsTrack) ;; groups=Factor or vector used to group samples in DataTrack for color-coding or aggregation ;; collapse=Logical parameter to enable or disable collapsing of overlapping features at low resolutions ;; window=Integer or character controlling binning/running window operations for data summarization in DataTrack ;; importFunction=User-defined function to parse non-standard files into GRanges objects ;; stream=Logical flag indicating whether data should be streamed off an indexed file on the fly ;; reverseStrand=Logical parameter to plot tracks in the 3' -> 5' direction>
- alternatives: <rtracklayer=Used to connect to online genome browsers (like UCSC) from within R, but lacks Gviz's flexibility to plot large numeric data in a multitude of different ways ;; GenomeGraphs=An older package on which Gviz is loosely based, but Gviz has a restructured class hierarchy and plotting methods for better performance and flexibility>
- when_to_use: <When integrating and visualizing diverse genomic data types (e.g., RNA-seq alignments, ChIP-seq coverage, microarray probes, gene models, CpG islands) along a shared genomic coordinate system for publication-quality figures.>
- pitfalls: <UCSC Chromosome Naming=By default, Gviz enforces UCSC chromosome naming (starting with "chr"). If using non-UCSC names, options(ucscChromosomeNames=FALSE) must be set ;; Slow Online Queries=Fetching data for IdeogramTrack or BiomartGeneRegionTrack from online servers (UCSC/Ensembl) can be slow or fail due to server load; local caching or local data sources should be used where possible ;; ReferenceDataTrack Length=Calling length() on a ReferenceDataTrack (created from streaming files like BAM) almost always returns 0 because data is only realized during plotting ;; Overplotting at Low Resolution=Features closer than 1 pixel will overlap or disappear unless collapse = TRUE and appropriate min.width / min.distance are set ;; Feature Name Conflicts=Custom feature names for color-coding in AnnotationTrack must not conflict with existing display parameter names in Gviz>

workflows.name: numeric_data_visualization
workflows.intent: Visualize numeric genomic data (e.g., microarray signals, custom scores, or bedGraph files) using various plot types and grouping.
input: twoGroups (GRanges object containing numeric metadata columns)
bgFile.bedGraph (bedGraph file containing genomic coordinates and a single numeric score column)
workflows.stages: 1. Load genomic coordinates and numeric data ;; 2. Construct a DataTrack object ;; 3. Plot the track using plotTracks with specific visualization types (e.g., histogram, boxplot, heatmap) ;; 4. Group data and add a legend
workflows.code:
data(twoGroups)
dTrack <- DataTrack(twoGroups, name = "uniform")
plotTracks(dTrack)
plotTracks(dTrack, type = c("boxplot", "a", "g"))
plotTracks(dTrack, type = c("heatmap"), showSampleNames = TRUE, cex.sampleNames = 0.6)
plotTracks(dTrack, groups = rep(c("control", "treated"), each = 3), type = c("a", "p", "confint"))
plotTracks(dTrack, groups = rep(c("control", "treated"), each = 3), type = c("a", "p"), legend = TRUE)

bgFile <- system.file("extdata/test.bedGraph", package = "Gviz")
dTrack2 <- DataTrack(range = bgFile, genome = "hg19", type = "l", chromosome = "chr19", name = "bedGraph")
plotTracks(dTrack2)

workflows.name: gene_region_visualization
workflows.intent: Visualize gene models and transcripts from local data frames or TxDb objects.
input: geneModels (data.frame containing gene model coordinates and identifiers)
hg19_knownGene_sample.sqlite (TxDb database file containing transcript and exon coordinates)
workflows.stages: 1. Load gene model data or connect to a TxDb database ;; 2. Construct a GeneRegionTrack ;; 3. Customize transcript annotations and collapsing options ;; 4. Plot the track along with reference tracks (axis, ideogram)
workflows.code:
data(geneModels)
grtrack <- GeneRegionTrack(geneModels, genome = gen, chromosome = chr, name = "Gene Model")
plotTracks(list(itrack, gtrack, atrack, grtrack))
plotTracks(grtrack, transcriptAnnotation = "symbol")
plotTracks(grtrack, collapseTranscripts = TRUE, shape = "arrow", transcriptAnnotation = "symbol")

library(GenomicFeatures)
samplefile <- system.file("extdata", "hg19_knownGene_sample.sqlite", package = "GenomicFeatures")
txdb <- loadDb(samplefile)
GeneRegionTrack(txdb)
txTr <- GeneRegionTrack(txdb, chromosome = "chr6", start = 35000000,  end = 40000000)
plotTracks(txTr)

workflows.name: sequence_alignment_visualization
workflows.intent: Visualize next-generation sequencing alignments from BAM files, including coverage, pileups, and sashimi junction plots.
workflows.stages: 1. Specify the path to the BAM file ;; 2. Construct an AlignmentsTrack object ;; 3. Plot the alignments using different visualization types (coverage, pileup, sashimi)
workflows.code:
afrom <- 2960000
ato <- 3160000
alTrack <- AlignmentsTrack(
  system.file(package = "Gviz", "extdata", "gapped.bam"), 
  isPaired = TRUE)
plotTracks(c(bmt, alTrack), from = afrom, to = ato, chromosome = "chr12")
plotTracks(c(bmt, alTrack), from = afrom, to = ato, chromosome = "chr12", min.height = 0, coverageHeight = 0.08, minCoverageHeight = 0)
plotTracks(c(alTrack, bmt), from = afrom, to = ato, chromosome = "chr12", type = "coverage")
plotTracks(c(bmt, alTrack), from = afrom + 12700, to = afrom + 15200, chromosome = "chr12", type = c("coverage", "sashimi"))
